headline: The Democratic sweep turned into the worst AI-chip sell-off since 2020: semis ETF -11.2% on the day, -29.2% on the month, and the damage has spread to grid and industrials.
regime: Nasdaq -5.5% and the semis ETF -11.2% on the day, -11.9% and -29.2% on the month; VIX 26.58 (+36.9% on five days). Every AI segment is down 17-34% on five days; only hyperscalers (-2.6%) held, and the 10-year eased to 4.84% while crude is near $91. Last session's grid and cooling leadership is gone (grid -17.6%, cooling -24.7% on five days), so this is a policy-and-positioning de-risking, not a read on orders: company prints (Quanta, Supermicro, Cloudflare) are still strong.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Quanta raised 2026 revenue guidance on a strong third quarter (0457b4c1b63e)
Bloom signed a 900 MW onsite power deal with NTT DATA, yet fell 16% (de4bd90b0048)
Against: Vertiv -14%, Quanta -12%, Powell -12.6% in a day as the sell-off hit industrials (ba0d098f03e6, 6d78534ca7de)
Against: GE Vernova faces a data-centre permitting pause (c974bb29aad5)
theses.change_note: -8: demand evidence is intact but the segments lost the five-day leadership and policy now targets build-out speed, which is the constraint itself.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Super Micro: Q1 sales $19.95bn, net income $1.59bn, higher 2027 outlook (2153f548cdfa)
Applied Optoelectronics: sixth record quarter, but shares fell 10% on weak Q4 guidance and 28% gross margin (7f22c236cbab, ee55114ce494)
Against: Microsoft delayed AI infrastructure deliveries at Iren; Micron's Taiwan fab delayed (39dba8e44b37, f59ab62cd957)
Against: compute -25% and foundry equipment -24.6% on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -8: demand prints hold, but delivery delays and guidance misses suggest supply, not demand, is the limit, and the price action shows doubt on duration.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Iren moved its $4bn AI cloud goal into 2027 with $6bn of capex unfunded and a $263m net loss (d4d482d7a172, 5dc9dde80b45)
CleanSpark -17% and Iren -17% as bitcoin fell below $76,000 (c60889cbf7ab)
Microsoft tightened oversight of Iren after delivery issues (8ca0605e544e)
Against: Iren rose 18% premarket on AI cloud revenue nearly tripling and investment-grade counterparties (da6cf588a387, a248aa118cde)
theses.change_note: +2: delays, unfunded capex and a customer tightening oversight, with the group -38% on the month; the Iren pop is a bounce, not a fix.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Micron is down over 40% from its June record after a 17% day (68065dc6d74c, f59ab62cd957)
Against: memory -33.7% on five days, SK Hynix -11.7% and Kospi sinking (e7212ca5ce8a, 9711899d0c5a)
Against: Micron's Taiwan construction delay and a union demand are a real operating risk (865fb763a45f)
theses.change_note: -8: the worst segment on five days with a company-specific supply hit; valuation support alone is not enough to hold the old level.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Argument that slower AI spending lets hyperscalers repair balance sheets (346f3733071d)
Oracle -17.5% on five days, the worst hyperscaler (digest segments)
Against: hyperscalers only -2.6% on five days and Amazon +6.7%, the market sees them as the safer side (80442cc1474a)
theses.change_note: -8: capex curbs would ease the cash squeeze and the market is rewarding the group; the thesis now cuts the other way for the strongest balance sheets.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Semis ETF -29.2% and Nasdaq -11.9% on the month; VIX up 77% on the month (digest tape)
Nvidia in bear territory; Nasdaq in correction (e771d9230122, 1ea0d18dcf08)
Against: the 10-year eased to 4.84% and futures bounced Friday pre-bell (df7bdcb58685, f02b110b358a)
theses.change_note: +8: the crowded-positioning unwind is now a rout; the easing 10-year is the only relief.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: The market reads a Democratic Congress as less AI spending; the sell-off spread to industrials (5c28c0a448c1, bdc319c89c9b)
Texas governor-elect says community approval must come before data centres (4ddca713a3a3)
GE Vernova faces a permitting-pause risk (c974bb29aad5)
Against: she is not ideologically opposed to data centres; no legislation exists yet (4ddca713a3a3)
theses.change_note: +32: the Nov 4 shrug became a two-day, market-wide repricing; still no concrete law, so confidence stays below the evidence of price damage.

compute.note: -25% on five days, Marvell -38.8%; demand is intact but this is a falling knife.

foundry_equipment.note: -24.6% on five days; cheap on forward earnings, buy only quality with cash flow.

memory_storage.note: -33.7% on five days with a Micron fab delay; wait for the cycle evidence.

networking_optical.note: -30.9% on five days; Arista holds best, Lumentum -44.6%, thin margins at AOI.

servers.note: Super Micro beat, but Dell -33.4% on five days.

power_nuclear.note: Talen -9.3% is the best in a falling group; developers still burn cash.

grid_electrical.note: Hubbell -4.4% held up; Quanta raised guidance, so the price drop is policy fear.

cooling_thermal.note: Trane -9.0% held; Modine -34.2% shows weaker names break.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Iren delays and unfunded capex; Equinix -3.8% is the only sturdy one.

hyperscalers.note: Only segment that held (-2.6%); Amazon +6.7%, Oracle -17.5%.

ai_software.note: -19.5% on five days; ServiceNow -6.7% is the best, Datadog -34.3%.

risks: Concrete state or federal data-centre legislation would hit orders for grid, cooling and neocloud names.
Forced selling and leverage in a -29% month could push the semis ETF past -35% before it stabilises.
Oil near $91-100 with Iran war risk keeps inflation and the 10-year sticky.
Neocloud funding stress, with Iren's $6bn unfunded capex, could cut GPU and power orders.
Today's October jobs report could move the 10-year in either direction.
watch: Whether Friday's pre-bell bounce holds into the close, or the sell-off resumes.
The October jobs report and the 10-year against 5%.
Any named data-centre bills or moratoria in Texas and other states.
Whether grid and cooling prints (PPL today, Vertiv follow-through) keep beating despite the price drop.
Micron's Taiwan fab timeline and Korean memory stocks after the 'Black Friday' drop.
